title: Install velocity — Sprint 11 blockers and weekly log
content:
Summary (week of 2026-03-05 to 2026-03-12)

This doc is the working weekly log for Sprint 11 install velocity and the set of persistent customer blockers affecting VPC and on-prem rollouts. It captures standup highlights, per-customer blocker states, short technical notes, and clear action items/owners. Use this as the authoritative list for tactical follow-ups this week.

Attendance (recurring standup): Priya, Miguel, Hannah, Samir, Evan, Jia; ad-hoc: Solutions eng reps from customer CTX and ZetaBank.

High-level metrics (Sprint 11):
- Scheduled installs: 9 (5 VPC, 4 on-prem)
- Completed installs: 4
- Blocked / delayed: 5
- Median time-to-unblock (for resolved): 14 hours
- Mean time-to-first-response (SRE/SE): ~35 minutes during business hours

Top cross-cutting themes this week:
- Network / MTU mismatches on customer edge routers (2 installs) causing large payload failures on model downloads.
- KMS integration failures where HSM certs are rejected by the customer's gateway (ZetaBank).
- Driver mismatch on customer on-prem GPU servers (NVIDIA driver < required version) — requires scheduled maintenance window.
- SELinux/enforced mode on a hardened image blocked runtime binding (Delta Retail).
- DNS split-horizon + internal NTP drift causing token validation to intermittently fail.

Per-customer breakdown

1) Acme Health (VPC) — status: blocked (network)
- Symptoms: model shard download stalls at ~60% and then times out. Replays show packets fragmented; kernel reports PMTU blackhole.
- Investigation notes: Customer edge device had MTU 1406 due to PPPoE; internal overlay expects 1500. TCP MSS clamping not enabled.
- Temporary mitigations tried: MFU workaround at load-balancer (reduced chunk size) succeeded for a single session but not a long-term fix.
- Action items: Miguel -> PD-8134 (JIRA) to capture permanent mitigation (enable MSS clamp or add reassembly proxy). SEs to request customer change during maintenance window. ETA: 48–72 hours pending customer ops approval.

2) Delta Retail (on-prem) — status: partial (blocked by SELinux)
- Symptoms: container fails to bind to /dev/nvidiactl in enforcing SELinux mode; runtime logs show AVC denials.
- Investigation notes: Delta uses CIS-hardened image with custom policy that denies bind on /dev. We attempted to load a permissive module but customer policy prevents module loading without elevated change requests.
- Workaround: start container with --security-opt label:disable (requires change approval) — not acceptable for compliance.
- Action items: Hannah -> work with SE (Liam) to produce a minimal SELinux policy patch that Delta can review. Create PD-8151 for tracking. ETA: tentative 1 week (policy + customer approval).

3) ZetaBank (VPC, high priority) — status: blocked (KMS/HSM handshake)
- Symptoms: KMS client cannot establish TLS session with customer HSM; TLS handshake fails at certificate verification step.
- Notes: Customer HSM presents RSA cert with PKCS#11 pin policy; our client attempts to validate chain but fails due to missing intermediate in their chain store.
- Quick test: loaded their intermediate in a test container — handshake succeeded. However customer policy forbids adding intermediates; they want HSM vendor to re-issue chain.
- Action items: Priya to coordinate escalation with CSM and legal for expedited vendor change or temporary allowlist. Evan to prepare fallback plan: encrypted-at-rest with customer-managed envelope keys (papered exception). ETA: working through vendor — 5 business days expected.

4) ThetaComm (on-prem, small PoC) — status: progressing
- Symptoms: initial setup completed, minor issue with host firewall blocking 443 egress to S3-like object store.
- Resolution: Samir guided host rule change; PoC containers are running. Remaining: telemetry sampling config (reduce to 10% for PoC).
- Action items: Samir to close ticket after telemetry config is applied. ETA: 24–48 hours.

5) NovaRetail (VPC) — status: delayed (ops calendar conflict)
- Reason: Customer has a scheduled data center migration; install deferred. SEs notified.
- Action items: schedule new window with Customer Success; no engineering work required until date confirmed.

Technical deep-dive notes (for implementers)
- MTU/packet fragmentation: prefer MSS clamping on edge devices for immediate relief; long-term add a reassembly proxy in the egress path that can accept fragmented shards and reassemble before passing to runtime. TLDR: avoid relying on jumbo frames across customer-managed WAN.
- NVIDIA driver mismatch: runtime requires driver >= 530.x for our optimized kernels. When driver < required, observed segmentation faults in fused attention kernels. We should add a preflight check script to the installer that validates driver and kernel module compatibility and outputs clear remediation steps.
- SELinux: create a vendor-neutral policy fragment (redwood-selinux-shim) that defines minimal allow rules for /dev and /sysfs interactions instead of instructing customers to disable enforcement.
- KMS/HSM: add a diagnostic harness to the installer that performs certificate chain verification and reports missing intermediates early in the preflight. This will reduce back-and-forth with vendor ops.

Recent standup log excerpts (timestamps local)
- 2026-03-08 09:15 — Priya: "Acme Health still blocked, Miguel you on the MSS clamp doc?" Miguel: "Drafted, pushing to PD-8134. Waiting for customer netops."
- 2026-03-09 14:40 — Hannah: "Delta Retail policy team wants example SELinux policy. I have minimal patch, will run by compliance."
- 2026-03-10 11:05 — Samir: "ThetaComm firewall change done; telemetry to be reduced."
- 2026-03-11 16:30 — Evan: "ZetaBank handed off to vendor; legal loop requested expedited review for temporary exception."

Outstanding decisions required from Product/Infra
- Approve adding preflight GPU/driver check to on-prem installer (low risk, high value). Product: decision required this week.
- Prioritize building KMS chain-check harness into the next private-deploy maintenance release. This is security-sensitive so coordinate with security team.
- Approve creation of 'redwood-selinux-shim' artifact and a short policy FAQ for customers.

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Miguel Alvarez — PD-8134: MSS clamp playbook + request template for customer netops (due 2026-03-14).
- Hannah Li — PD-8151: Minimal SELinux policy fragment + test harness (due 2026-03-19).
- Priya Shah — Coordinate escalation for ZetaBank KMS vendor change; draft temporary allowlist exception (due 2026-03-17).
- Samir Patel — Close ThetaComm telemetry ticket and verify PoC stability (due 2026-03-06).
- Evan Brooks — Prepare fallback envelope-key plan and legal language for exception (due 2026-03-16).

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Multiple high-priority customers blocked by non-Redwood infra (edge routers, HSM vendor). Mitigation: build better preflight diagnostics and a short SOP for rapid escalation to sales/legal.
- Risk: Installer changes may increase QA surface area. Mitigation: keep preflight checks non-destructive and optional behind a feature flag for Private releases.

Notes / Questions for next leadership sync
- Do we want to mandate an install preflight checklist for every on-prem engagement? (Pro: reduces elbow grease; Con: small friction).
- Is there budget to spin up a small field-eng team (2 FTE) dedicated to first-10-installs friction? This could materially increase velocity.

Appendix: quick links
- PD runbook (confluence): private-deploy-runbook-v2
- Current ticket list: PD-8134, PD-8151, PD-8169 (driver mismatch), PD-8190 (NTP/dns)

End of log.

If you are owner of an action item, please update the corresponding JIRA and ping #private-deploy-standup-thread when you move to 'in-progress' or 'resolved'.
